text.p: Cash squeeze continuing since last Friday in the Turkish market due to hefty mid-month public salary payments prompted heavy central bank funding on Monday, bankers said.
The central bank lent 20.4 trillion lira at 72 percent overnight to relieve cash demand and also funded the banks 25.1 trillion lira at 67 percent via tmrw/next on expected cash squeeze on Tuesday.
The average overnight money rate rose to 71.81 percent from 68.79 percent on Friday and the average repo rate also went up to 69.40 percent versus 58.92 percent in line with the cash shortage.
Bond demand continued despite cash shortage. Banks prefered to buy outstanding papers on the secondary market amid expectations that inflation-indexed bonds would be launched this week, bankers said.
But the Treasury announced a regular 13-month bond auction for Tuesday with Wednesday value when the Treasury has 90 trillion lira of bond redemption.
The most actively traded paper was December 10,1997 at 93.11 percent yield which fell 0.38 points from Friday.
The Turkish lira slightly firmed to 125,300 against teh dollar from 125,310 at Friday's close due to tight liquidity and a weak dollar against the mark.
